title: Introduction to the Dynamic Nelson-Siegel Model
text: Nelson-Siegel model parsimonious parametric model yield curve. expresses yield maturity three factors: y(m)=β1+β2(1−e−λmλm)+β3(1−e−λmλm−e−λm)y(m) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m}\right) + \beta_3 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m} - e^{-\lambda m}\right) y(m)y(m) yield maturity mm, β1\beta_1 long-term level interest rates, β2\beta_2 slope, short-term minus long-term, β3\beta_3 curvature, size hump, λ\lambda controls fast factor loadings decay. loadings give factor interpretation: level loads equally every maturity, slope loads short end decays zero, curvature peaks somewhere middle.

text: Nelson-Siegel model expresses yield curve : $$y(m) = \beta_1 + \beta_2 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m}\right) + \beta_3 \left(\frac{1-e^{-\lambda m}}{\lambda m} - e^{-\lambda m}\right)$$ \(m\) maturity, \(\beta_1\), \(\beta_2\), \(\beta_3\) represent level, slope, curvature factors, respectively, \(\lambda\) controls decay rate factor loadings. Dynamic Nelson-Siegel model, factors follow mean-reverting stochastic process: $$d\beta(t) = \kappa(\theta - \beta(t))dt + \sigma dW(t)$$ \(\kappa\) speed mean reversion, \(\theta\) long-run mean, \(\sigma\) volatility, \(W(t)\) Wiener process.
